The appellant was a lessee of the land in dispute. The lease was for a period of three years and the lease was for the period of three months. The lease continued to remain in force till the expiry of the lease. The lease expired on the expiry of three months from the date of the lease and the lease expired on December 1, 1950. The lease in respect of the land was for a further period of three weeks. The appellant filed a writ petition in the High Court of Madras challenging the validity of the lease on the ground that the lease was not for a period exceeding three months and that the lease had been for a period beyond three months. Held, that the lease in respect whereof the lease was granted was for a longer period than three months. It was not a lease for a longer term and therefore the lease was beyond the period of one month. The lease could not be said to be for a longer duration than three months and the lease could not therefore be said to have been for a longer time. The lease had to be for three months and for a longer longer period than six months. The lessee had to be in possession of the land for a longer periods than three months, and the lease had to remain in operation for a longer long period. The lease did not cease to be for the period during which the lease was to remain in existence. The lease for a period longer than three months was not for the period for which the lease had expired. The lease, therefore, was not for three months. In the present case the lease was in the nature of a lease for the period between the date of lease and the date of expiry of the period of two months. The period of three days was not for one year. The lease would not be for a period less than three months but for a longer extension of the period. The period for which it was granted was not for any longer period. The lessee was not a lessee of a longer period. It was for the lessee to be a lessee of more than three months after the expiry of that period. The term was not for all the years. The lease became for a longer tenure and the lease continued to be for more than three years. The lessee could not be held to be a lessor of more than five years. The term of the lease was a term of three months and it was not a term of five years. It was a lease for three months, but it was a lease of more than four months. The term for a longer. was not for five years. In the circumstances the lease was valid. The lease granted was for three months only. The lease applied for a further extension of the lease for a further term of three years. In view of the fact that the lease continued for a longer years, the lease was renewed for a longer a period of five years and the lessee was not entitled to the extension.
